Let  
\[
\chi(a)=\left(\frac ap\right),\qquad n=\frac{p-1}{2}.
\]
We need
\[
P_p=\prod_{k=1}^n \chi(k^2+k+1)
=\chi\!\left(\prod_{k=1}^n(k^2+k+1)\right),
\]
unless one factor is \(0\).

If \(p\equiv1\pmod 3\), then \(\mathbb F_p^\times\) contains nontrivial cube roots of unity, so \(x^2+x+1\) has two roots modulo \(p\). If their least positive representatives are \(r,s\), then
\[
r+s\equiv -1\pmod p,
\]
and since \(1\le r,s\le p-1\), actually \(r+s=p-1\). Hence at least one of \(r,s\) lies in \(\{1,\dots,n\}\), so one factor is \(0\). Thus
\[
P_p=0\qquad(p\equiv1\pmod3).
\]

Now assume \(p\equiv2\pmod3\). Let \(\alpha\) be a root of \(x^2+x+1\) in \(\mathbb F_{p^2}\). Then \(\alpha^p=\alpha^2=-1-\alpha\). Define
\[
Q(x)=\prod_{k=1}^n(x-k).
\]
Since
\[
k^2+k+1=(k-\alpha)(k-\alpha^p),
\]
we have
\[
B:=\prod_{k=1}^n(k^2+k+1)=Q(\alpha)Q(\alpha^p).
\]

The roots of \(Q(x)Q(-1-x)\) are \(1,\dots,p-2\), with \(n\) repeated, and its leading coefficient is \((-1)^n\). Hence
\[
Q(x)Q(-1-x)=(-1)^n(x-n)\frac{x^{p-1}-1}{x+1}.
\]
Evaluating at \(x=\alpha\), using \(\alpha^p=\alpha^2\), gives \(\alpha^{p-1}=\alpha\), so
\[
B=(-1)^n(\alpha-n)\frac{\alpha-1}{\alpha+1}.
\]
Since \(n\equiv -\frac12\pmod p\),
\[
(\alpha-n)\frac{\alpha-1}{\alpha+1}
=\left(\alpha+\frac12\right)\frac{\alpha-1}{\alpha+1}
=-\frac32,
\]
using \(\alpha^2+\alpha+1=0\). Therefore
\[
B\equiv (-1)^{n+1}\frac32\pmod p.
\]
When \(p\equiv2\pmod3\), the factor \(\chi((-1)^{n+1})\) is always \(1\), so
\[
P_p=\chi(B)=\chi\left(\frac32\right)=\chi(6).
\]

Thus
\[
\boxed{
P_p=
\begin{cases}
0,& p\equiv 1\pmod 3,\\[2mm]
\left(\dfrac{6}{p}\right),& p\equiv 2\pmod 3.
\end{cases}}
\]

Equivalently, for \(p>3\),
\[
P_p=
\begin{cases}
0,& p\equiv 1,7,13,19\pmod{24},\\
1,& p\equiv 5,23\pmod{24},\\
-1,& p\equiv 11,17\pmod{24}.
\end{cases}
\]
